title: Module 3: Claude Code, MCP & Integration
subtitle: from your machine to real systems

beats.narration: Module three moves the work into your terminal. Claude Code runs the same model, and the same agent loop you built in module two, but adds three things around it: a permission layer that gates every action, a configuration system, and team-oriented sharing. Plus MCP, the protocol for connecting to external services securely. And it's all organized around one recurring problem: code that works on your machine now has to hold up when someone else runs it, against real company systems.

items.text: a permission layer on every action

elements.text: "works on my machine" → must survive everyone else's

beats.narration: Six skills by the end. Run the explore, plan, code loop, under a permission mode matched to the risk of the work. Review AI-generated code with calibrated trust, and place human gates where wrong calls are expensive. Give the agent durable project context: CLAUDE dot M D, rules files, hooks, and subagents. Package a workflow as skills, commands, and plugins that teammates can install. Build an MCP server, and pick its transport and scope. And connect Claude to enterprise systems with authentication a regulated customer will accept.

Every convenience on your machine can become a failure on someone else's: the permission mode that deletes out-of-scope files, the rule buried under eight hundred lines, the skill pointing at a path only you have, the committed key that leaks in hours. This module teaches which configuration decision prevents which failure. Let's start with permissions.
